_readme: A REGISTER, NOT A CENSUS. Every other number in this project is something the collector saw
for itself and can show you a raw capture for. Nothing in this file is. These are facts read
out of company filings, exchange announcements and the trade press, typed in by hand, each
carrying the date it was true, how sure we are, and where it came from.
Consequently: a missing count is written as null and never guessed, and 'no_evidence' means
we did not find a presence, NOT that there is none. Those are different claims and the
register refuses to blur them.
WHAT GETS A ROW. Two tests, and only two: the chain originates in China, and there is
evidence it trades in a market this project covers. Whether we can COLLECT it is not a test.
A register that admitted only the chains with a convenient locator would describe the subset
that is easy to scrape and call it the world — and it would quietly drop Pop Mart, Cotti and
Yang's Braised Chicken, which are among the most interesting entries in it. Collectability
decides the METHOD (a daily adapter, or a hand-typed row with its reason recorded), never the
membership. Size in China is not a test either: a chain with 20,000 domestic stores and no
foreign shopfront belongs to a different subject.
ORIGIN AND DESTINATION ARE DIFFERENT AXES, which is what lets Hong Kong sit in this list.
The project collects chains that ORIGINATE in China; Taiwanese and Hong Kong brands
are out of scope as origins. Hong Kong as a DESTINATION is another matter: it is part of
China politically and a separate retail market practically — its own currency, rents, labour
market, tastes and regulator. A Zhengzhou chain opening in Mong Kok is making the same kind
of bet it makes in Singapore, at smaller scale. The register says so and lets the reader
disagree, rather than deciding the question by leaving the row out.
Reviewed periodically rather than daily — `python -m chain_atlas register --stale` lists
what has not been looked at in 90 days.

Count read on 21 Sep 2026 from Super Hi's own /eportal/earth/list endpoint, which backs the 'Global Stores' panel on its corporate site. CAVEAT WORTH KEEPING: the field names are swapped in their CMS — the store count sits in a field called `ownedCountries` and the city count in `ownedCities`. Read literally it is nonsense (Singapore in 17 countries). The reading used here is checked by arithmetic: the second field sums to 114 across 14 countries, against the site's own headline of '110+ global stores' in '14 operating countries'. The Cambodia row is corrupt — the global total was typed into its city field — and is ignored. Super Hi's largest single market, more than 18% of its overseas restaurants.
